title: Haricots verts à la française
subtitle: French-style green beans with lettuce, onion, and butter
excerpt: Thin French green beans braised slowly in butter with little onions, shredded lettuce, and a splash of stock until tender and lightly glazed. A classic way to cook haricots verts in the French style.
sourceNotes: Haricots verts à la française is a classic French braised vegetable method. The technique of braising green vegetables with butter, pearl onions, and lettuce appears in Escoffier's Le Guide Culinaire (1903) and in Larousse Gastronomique (1938). Both are available as public-domain or widely-cited historical culinary references.

content.text: This is not the same thing as blanching green beans and finishing them in butter. À la française means braising: the beans cook slowly in a covered pan with onions, a little lettuce, butter, and a small amount of liquid. The result is softer than blanched beans, sweeter, and with a light buttery glaze. It is the French country way of cooking green vegetables, and it tastes much better than its simplicity suggests.

items.prepNote: peeled, or use small shallots halved

content.text: Melt the butter in a wide, heavy saucepan or sauté pan over medium heat. Add the pearl onions and a pinch of sugar. Cook, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes until they start to colour lightly.
Add the green beans and stir to coat in the butter. Pour in the stock. Add the shredded lettuce and season with salt and pepper. Stir briefly, then cover the pan tightly.

Cook over a moderate heat for 12 to 15 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally, until the beans are tender and most of the liquid has been absorbed or evaporated. Uncover for the last 2 minutes to reduce any remaining liquid to a glaze.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: Beans are still firm after 15 minutes
items.cause: Beans too thick, or heat too low
items.fix: The very thin haricots verts variety works best. If using thicker beans, increase cooking time. Add a splash more stock if the pan dries before the beans are cooked.

items.cause: Lettuce released water faster than it evaporated
items.fix: Uncover and increase the heat for 3 to 4 minutes to reduce the liquid to a glaze.

content.text: The à la française method of braising peas, beans, or lettuce with butter and small onions is a cornerstone of French home cooking. It appears in cookbooks from the Loire Valley and the Paris basin, regions where market gardens have supplied haricots verts to kitchens since the seventeenth century. The dish is served alongside roast chicken, grilled lamb chops, or a simple piece of pan-roasted fish. It is the kind of side dish that makes the rest of the plate taste better.
